items.title: GTA 6 Skipping PC At Launch And Having No Online Right Away Is Good, Helldivers Boss Says
items.summary: The CEO of Helldivers studio Arrowhead Game Studios has commented on the upcoming launch of GTA 6 , saying he'

content.v: The CEO of Helldivers studio Arrowhead Game Studios has commented on the upcoming launch of GTA 6 , saying he's happy there will be no PC version or online mode at launch, because that will help Helldivers 2 "keep crushing it."

In a statement to press, Sham Jorjani said Rockstar makes "ridiculous, high-effort stuff, and it's awesome that games like this get made." He said he's selfishly happy that the game won't be on PC at launch, nor will there be an online mode right away.
"It means Helldivers 2 gets to keep crushing it in our own space, and is also why it won’t be the all consuming behemoth everyone’s worried about," he said.

Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 will launch on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, but the developer has not said a word about a possible PC edition. Additionally, Rockstar has said GTA 6 is a "single-player experience," but the company has not confirmed outright that there won't be an online mode at launch.

It's expected Rockstar will evolve GTA Online in some form for GTA 6 , but we don't know anything about that yet. With GTA 5, the game launched first on console before later coming to PC. For GTA 6, it's expected the game will also eventually come to PC. Additionally, it won't be unprecedented if GTA 6 launches with no online mode, as GTA 5 also launched without one.
Jorjani went on to say Rockstar has "the brand power to confidently take their time and run their classic play," as opposed to chasing trends and pivoting like some other developers do.
"They have the confidence and freedom to spend a decade doing things the old-school way because they know the core game will deliver. It’s going to raise the bar for sure," he said.
The "Extended Look" for GTA 6 aired today, August 27, on Netflix. For more, be sure to read GameSpot’s breakdown of how to watch and what to expect from the GTA 6 Extended Look event .
The Netflix event comes after GTA 6 has suffered numerous, significant gameplay leaks. Rockstar reacted to the scandal, saying the leaks are “heartbreaking” for the developers .
GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It’s coming to market with an incredible amount of hype behind it, in part because fans have been waiting 13 years for the sequel to GTA 5 .

items.title: You Can Pet (And Scold, You Monster) The Dog In GTA 6
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI had its big debut on Netflix today, and as part of the opening sequence we got confirmatio

content.v: Grand Theft Auto VI had its big debut on Netflix today, and as part of the opening sequence we got confirmation that there will be very good boys, by which I mean dogs, and you can interact them in a few different ways.

When exploring an apartment complex for a package pickup, Jason and Lucia come across a dog in the hallway. Jason leans over to interact, allowing you to pet the dog, as we've come to expect in video games. But two other options were also notable: Scold, and Study.

Scolding a dog is probably exactly what it sounds like, though we didn't see it in action. Maybe there's a dog behavior mechanic and scolding helps steer them right? The Study option appears borrowed from Red Dead Redemption 2, which allowed you to study wild animals. That may indicate GTA 6 will allow you to study a variety of creatures, not just dogs. A New York Times report further detailed that you can buy treats for dogs at shops and give them out.

items.title: ‘It’s a Step Forward in All Respects’ – Exclusive GTA 6 Interview
items.summary: Our exclusive interview with Rockstar’s Rob Nelson reveals how GTA 6 aims to be “a step forward in all respect

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/27/mega-4-1787854867266.jpeg

The whole world is going feral as Grand Theft Auto 6's November release date approaches, desperate for even the tiniest of details. Meanwhile Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, is a man who has had to keep all those details secret for a very long time.
Finally, when I sat down in his office in the Scottish capital of Edinburgh for an exclusive IGN interview, he was able to spill some of those GTA 6 secrets for the very first time.

"I think the challenge for us on this game is the same as it is on any new game for us,” says Nelson. “How do we evolve and build upon the good things we have done before in all the ways these things need to evolve, but at the same time ensure that the game still has everything that made the previous games in this series resonate with people?"

The answer seems to be, for a large (if not the most) part, in creating a whole world that players can spend meaningful time in, engaging in fulfilling activities that go beyond simply grinding sidequests for cash or trying to boost stats to power through the main story. The setting of Leonida is begging to be explored and experienced by the player.
"The game is so big, I don’t know that there’s anybody on the team that knows all of it," he says.
Making friends (or not) in Leonida

As we're talking, Nelson is multitasking, playing through a slice of Grand Theft Auto 6 that will go on to perfectly exemplify his point. It's dense with NPCs, traffic weaving through the streets, and opportunities for mayhem at every turn. And those people on the sidewalks? They're ready to cause all sorts of chaos.

"While we pushed interaction with NPCs as far as we could for Red Dead Redemption 2, with this game we are taking it much further,” he explains. "The team has done an incredible job to create all of this crazy dialogue, and you can stand there and listen to them, but we’ve tried to find a balance where if you stand too close to a group, they should notice that you're eavesdropping."

"So, if you stand there and try to listen to the whole thing, they'll often turn around, notice you and go, ‘Oh hey, can I help you?’ Or if you follow people for too long and too close so that they can hear you, they’ll go, ‘Oh, hey.’ Then they may be aggressive, or they may just want to get away from you. When we first started these ideas back on Red Dead Redemption 2, we thought if we could get it working there in a more sparsely populated world, we imagined what it might feel like at scale in a modern world. So it was one of the scary but very worthwhile and fun challenges we took on with this game."
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/27/mega-12-1787854498197.jpeg

According to Nelson, an epic amount of time, research and work went into populating the world, styling the NPCs so that every area of the world feels distinct. Rockstar even had a team in LA solely dedicated to NPC dialogue, which is how you end up with GTA gems like "you can use my balls like a punching bag" and "I can pee on you if you pay me."

The evolution of the world’s NPCs extend beyond banter, clothing, and mugging them for $5. It's one of the places where it’s clear that the development of Red Dead Redemption 2 has had a significant influence on GTA 6.

"This NPC interaction system is one that is returning and evolved from Red Dead Redemption 2,” says Nelson. “In the past, we’ve had systems where you can speak to NPCs, in Red Dead Redemption 1 and GTA 5 there were basic systems for interacting, but the interactions were very simple. But with Red Dead Redemption 2, we were finally able to incorporate the ability to interact with NPCs as a more fleshed-out system."

He specifically references the use of the left trigger, something that was once a binary system, and how the team had to adapt to allow for the more nuanced approach of using the trigger as a way to interact with the world without pulling out a weapon. That same system and the expertise around it have made their way into GTA 6.
"We have to do so much work in design, in code behaviors, in animation, in writing, to get these

interactions to feel believable," he says. "Now, everybody across all of these teams – across technical teams, animation teams, across design teams, across writing teams – need to in a way become students of human behavior. You find yourself watching how people behave out in the world and studying the rise and fall of a conversation as you pass two people."
GTA 6 on IGN: All Our Exclusive Stories
Criminology, GTA style

That detail and the specificity it allows for is supported by the new Criminal Profile system, a spiritual successor to Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor system. While it does dynamically alter based on activities that could be broadly considered “good” or “bad”, your profile is not there to encourage you to be a perfect citizen. This is a game about how much fun it can be to break the law, after all, but it’s up to you how maliciously violent you want to be about it.

"As much as possible, we tried to design the game so that you have options,” Nelson explains. “Things can escalate quite quickly if you want them to, or people who don’t want to escalate can try to avoid it. It’s not always possible. To me that supports the narrative.

"This is a story about a couple on the run. We have tried to make the systems and the design support our narrative when and wherever possible. Meaning, if you hit and run, commit a crime and run, get into trouble and move on before the cops get there, and you don’t start shooting people, don't start escalating – which you absolutely can do if you want to – but if you don’t, you’re generally going to be fine."

Nelson says the team began to experiment with the idea that you're not the only dangerous person in the world in Red Dead Redemption 2. In its lawless frontier you could be attacked by roving gangs, or start fights with people on the trails. GTA 6 builds new layers into those choices.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/27/mega-11-1787854457692.jpeg

"So, if you're doing things on mission that you are required to do – or you’re robbing places, or somebody comes and messes with you and you have to deal with them by smacking them down or whatever – that’s all fair game,” Nelson explains. “It's when you go beyond what is necessary on a consistent basis, or you do completely unnecessary stuff consistently, that you may start to sway your criminal profile in a certain direction."

"Maybe you care about that as a player, maybe you don’t. There is no right or wrong way to play this. To us, it's a very interesting concept. In previous games, you’re quite overpowered in the world compared to everyone else apart from the cops, which can be fun, but not as fun, I don’t think, as having a world where there may be other people that have impulses of their own and act upon you. You are still powerful and capable, but you are not the only one capable of violence or the only one with weapons or the only crazy person out there. It makes the world far more unpredictable and interesting."
Wanted and Busted

This new system exists alongside the iconic Wanted levels and risk of getting Busted. Again, further complexity has been added to these systems, but the same thrills of evading police helicopters, fleeing mayhem in sports cars, and getting into deeper and deeper trouble at every turn are still alive and well.

items.title: Rockstar Doesn’t Mind if You Dislike GTA 6’s Romantic Side: ‘Don’t Bother With It. Up to You’
items.summary: GTA 6 has a whole relationship system to increase Jason and Lucia’s bond, but it’s completely optional if you’

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/27/mega-3-1787855175829.jpeg

During an interview with IGN, Rob Nelson, the head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, explained the design decisions behind making Jason and Lucia's relationship key to the story but not to the gameplay mechanics.

"I have to say it feels great — if you are into it as a concept. Don’t bother with it if you aren’t. Up to you," said Nelson. Jason and Lucia will always have each other's backs in the story and during the action, but spending quality time together and nurturing the relationship? That's up to the player, and you won't be penalized if you're not interested in the sappy stuff.

"The narrative is structured in such a way that the circumstances they find themselves in require them to stay together for most of the story and work together. At the very least they will get through most things as partners in crime," explained Nelson.

"I don’t want to say too much more about this because I don’t want to spoil anything. It really adds a compelling element to things, and it’s one of the reasons we wanted to approach this sort of story, because it's completely different for us. Could we bring some sort of emotional resonance to GTA for people if they wanted to engage with it? Could we also provide mechanisms for people to just opt out of it if they're not into it? If they feel like, ‘I don't want a relationship in this?’ That's what we're going to find out. It's not something that we want to foist upon players."
For players that want to spend time together, the vast map of Leonida offers plenty of opportunities for the quality time Nelson mentioned.
"Robbing places together, or walking around, holding hands, going to a zoo, studying animals, going scuba diving, parachuting, walking on the beach, kayaking…," he said.

"When you bring them together, it feels like you’re a steward of their relationship, and you feel protective of them as a unit. But this is something we did not know when we started, and it really had to be something we felt our way through. But I will say that whether you’re getting in trouble, or you’re running from the cops, or getting in a car, or waiting for the other one — playing as them together feels very cool. It feels like you’re taking care of them, if that’s something you’re into."
Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released on November 19.
GTA 6 on IGN: All Our Exclusive Stories

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. items.title: ‘We Are Nervous!’ — Rockstar Knows the Pressure on GTA 6 to Be a Success
items.summary: We asked Rockstar how it’s dealing with the pressure of ensuring GTA 6 is a success after so many years of dev

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/27/gta6-nervous-news-1787849001685.jpg
It feels like the whole world is waiting to play GTA 6. And Rockstar knows it.

Ahead of the extended look that just debuted on Netflix, IGN had the chance to visit the developer and talk with Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North. Upon us mentioning just how each new Grand Theft Auto feels like a global cultural moment, he replies with a laugh, “No pressure.”

“I try not to think about it,” Nelson continues. “You’re aware of it, of course. But I think we just have to try and make something that we feel is innovating on what we’ve done previously, evolving it while still making it feel familiar.”

Rockstar knows that each and every scrap of information revealed about GTA 6 is analysed with a fine-tooth comb, and this recent extended look is certainly no different, as we’re given our biggest insight yet into the world, characters, and gameplay of this revisit to Vice City. It means each frame needs to be perfect, with every detail bound to be made into a list feature revealing new secrets about the game — exactly something we’ll be doing ourselves.

“It’s a hard thing,” Nelson explains. “As much pressure as we feel externally, I don’t think it can compare to the pressure we put on ourselves as a team. Everyone wants things to be perfect. We are nervous! Nervous, of course, but also excited to see how people respond to this video and then ultimately the game. It is definitely a step forward in all respects for us – the size of the world, and how deep it feels. It’s a bit of a shock when you get in there, and you see the density of the traffic, the density of population, and the fidelity of their responses to you.”

While we don’t as of yet know just how many people have pre-ordered GTA 6 ahead of its November 19 launch, we do know that the majority of players have opted for the more expensive $100 ultimate edition than the standard one. The boss of the game’s publisher, Take-Two, has described that price as a “bargain” as “Rockstar Games is known for over-delivering.” You can see why Nelson and company may well be feeling that pressure.

items.title: ‘Is It Four Characters Now?’ — Rockstar Briefly Thought About Doubling the Number of GTA 6 Protagonists
items.summary: Following GTA 5’s three playable characters, Rockstar considered putting four protagonists in GTA 6 before set

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/27/gta6-8-blogroll-1787855254976.jpg

Long before we knew that GTA 6 would be played from the perspective of dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, many were wondering just how many playable characters Rockstar’s latest would include. And it turns out that the answer wasn’t always two.

Grand Theft Auto 5 charted a new direction for the series by increasing the number of characters to three, where there had always been just one. Red Dead Redemption 2 does have multiple protagonists, but can never be switched between in the style of GTA 5 due to story reasons. It begged the question of which direction the developer would go when first designing 6.

IGN recently visited Rockstar North to speak with co-studio head Rob Nelson, who revealed discussions were had at one point in time regarding the number of characters increasing to four. But, ultimately, the team landed on one couple, with the bonds built between player and character at the foremost point of those discussions.

“As the narrative unfolds, we're quite conscious to try and make sure that players have enough time with each character,” says Nelson. “After doing GTA 5, we talked about different ideas of – do we do more characters? How do we follow up three characters? Is it four characters now? But we worried about diluting the amount of player time with each and therefore player connection with those characters. So we decided to step in this direction of two characters in a relationship.”

But then the question became: how do you make players feel like, ‘I love them both?’ Chemistry is a notoriously hard thing to do in any sort of entertainment. Either the characters and the actors that embody them have it – or they don't. Everyone involved worked at that pretty hard. I think we’ve got it. I think we’ve got enough reaction within our team internally to where they feel great as individuals and together.”

items.title: ‘We Have To Be Careful’ — Rockstar on GTA 6’s Approach to Satire
items.summary: Rockstar is still dedicated to making Grand Theft Auto a funny satire of modern America, but it’s being carefu

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/27/gta6-satire-news-1787848953836.jpg

Thirteen years is a long time. It can feel especially long when you’re developing a game in a series that loves nothing more than to satirize the times we live in. GTA 6 has the challenge, then, of not feeling out of touch with the world its trying to find the funny side of.

It’s something that Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North is astutely aware. “That’s a question a lot of people ask: how do you deal with satire in today’s world?” he told IGN on an exclusive visit to the developer’s Scottish office.

“I think there’s always stuff to satirize. As long as humans are humans, other humans will figure out ways to satirize what we do. For us, because we work on such a long development cycle, we have to not jump on stuff and instead choose our angle of approach carefully and decide what things are going to be a bit more timeless. We’re not a TV show coming out every week or every month. We have to be careful that what we’re choosing to satirize is not going to feel dated in a weird way. I think those broader things are OK to satirize, but very specific political issues or memes will date fast. Even the way our characters speak we think about it a lot, so that they're not using extremely contemporary slang. Even though our characters are a certain age, they need to feel somewhat timeless.”

Being able to feel a connection with the two protagonists is a huge part of Rockstars’s games. They are, typically, people commits crimes and doing horrible things to one another, so creating a warmth toward them is a real challenge. This is something that Rockstar has decades of experience doing by now, though. Making sure they feel true-to-life when talking, and giving them believable, and somewhat relatable backgrounds is a huge part of this.

“Jason and Lucia as characters have rich backstories that we sometimes explicitly talk about, sometimes just allude to,” Nelson reveals. “I think there is enough detail there if you want to pay attention, but we also have purposely left them with some room for interpretation so that hopefully the connection can be enhanced between the player and these characters. That is maybe as important as it has ever been for these characters in particular because I think for this story to work for you, for you to buy into this relationship, you have to be able to connect with them in some way. Hopefully a good number of people will feel like they can do that.”

Satire, nor characters, are the aspects that Rockstar settles on first when developing a new Grand Theft Auto game, though. The origin point is the world, and, in the case of GTA 6, a return to Vice City.

“A lot of people ask how do you think about satire and what angle to use? But satire is not usually the first thing that we think about, it’s something that develops,” Nelson explains. “The first thing we think about is where are we going to set it? – OK, Miami and Florida – Vice City and Leonida. Then we go there and start meeting with as many different people as we can. We start figuring out what sorts of experiences we want the player to have, and what places we want them to go, and what types of people we want them to meet. Then we figure out what’s a good character set to take the player through that? Those are the big things. Then, we ask, ‘What do we want to improve upon that we did before?’ Certainly choice. Another big thing is trying to connect who you are in the narrative with who you are in the open world as much as possible, so it feels like one singular experience.”

items.title: ‘It’s a Big Map, a Very Big Map’ – GTA 6 Is Rockstar’s Most Complex World Yet
items.summary: Rockstar explains how it has pushed current-gen technology to ensure GTA 6’s massive map is a step beyond Red

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/27/gta6-12-blogroll-1787855020965.jpg
When it comes to open-world games, and especially Rockstar’s, one of the biggest questions is always “how big is the map?” Well, when it comes to GTA 6 we now have a answer. Kind of.

The main stories of Rockstar games and the bombastic missions that they’re made up of are always a huge part of the allure of these now once-in-a-generation events, but there’s always plenty to do once those tales have ended. As with 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2, it will be no different in GTA 6.

“There is a whole other world in Red Dead Redemption 2, yes. GTA 6 is very much like that,” Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North, told IGN in an exclusive interview. “There's a whole lot of stuff that you discover emergently that we're not necessarily directing you to through objectives or blips or icons on a map as well. If you take a bit of time and explore you will be rewarded – a lot. It’s a big map, a very big map.”

To create such a large playground to play in takes a huge amount of time and effort, though, as well as the tools to build them with. This is where the power of the current generation of consoles comes into the picture, with Rockstar now able to push things even further than Red Dead Redemption 2 was able to go when it launched on PS4 and Xbox One.

“I think with Red Dead Redemption 2, we finally had the team and the tech and then took the time we needed to push the idea of making a fully realized consistent-feeling world further than we ever had,” Nelson explains. “With that game we took the time necessary to take advantage of that generation of hardware to maximize the quality of our open world population, design, and gameplay so that when you were riding from here to there in-game, you were constantly getting distracted and pulled in different directions. And then you could really get lost as that character in that place. That's when to me, these games can feel magical and create a sense of wonder that the world is alive – and you get these little shivers of ‘What’s happening?’

GTA 6 is a continuation of our team pushing in this direction – doing everything we possibly can to create the largest, deepest, most densely populated and complex world we have ever built for people to get lost in.”

One of the most noticeable improvements to the world of Leonida when compared to previous Grand Theft Auto locations, will be the people that populate. Thanks to the power of modern consoles, a far greater level of diversity will be seen when it comes to body shapes, height, and the way they move through Vice City and its surrounding areas.

“One of the coolest things about this game being developed from the ground up on this generation of hardware is taking advantage of all the memory that we have on the latest consoles combined with our teams’ experience doing this for so long together,” says Nelson.

“NPCs have more height differentiation and body shape differentiation than ever before, we could never have had this variety before because different body types had to share animation sets. So, if you had the same animation on the 5’6” person and the 6’2” person, they wouldn’t line up if they're fighting or sitting in cars—basically any interactions with each other or the environment. But on this game, the team worked out a system where they now retarget those animations on the fly. Now we have a huge variety of heights and shapes and it all works together because of what this team was able to pull off.”

items.title: 克里斯·罗伯茨表示，《星际公民》的《42 中队》再次推迟，这次是为了避免“GTA 6 的关注”
items.summary: The star-packed singleplayer space FPS, first planned for 2015, has missed another release window.

content.v: We see games getting delayed all the time, but today's delay is particularly notable because this particular game was first supposed to come out in, ooh, let me check... Yep. All the way back in 2015.

Squadron 42, the long-awaited, celebrity-packed episodic singleplayer component of Star Citizen has been delayed once again. And why? This time, according to game director Chris Roberts, it's to avoid the media hubbub around another oft-delayed game: GTA 6.
"At CitizenCon 2024 we announced we would ship in 2026. Our plan was to release in Q4 around IAE," Roberts said in a post on the RSI website.

"But much like the rest of the industry there is no way I want to launch my spiritual successor to Wing Commander, a game that has had twelve years of blood, sweat and tears invested into it (we started Squadron 42 development in 2014 as 2013 was opening studios, hiring people and getting the Hangar module out for Star Citizen) launching into the attention buzz saw of GTA 6.
"While GTA 6 isn’t launching on PC this November, pretty much all outlets and most content creators will be all over it, not leaving a lot of room for other coverage," Roberts said.
"We have taken a look at the release windows at the start of 2027, and decided that Q2 provides a better time for Squadron 42 to release."

Look, I dunno. Roberts isn't wrong: there will be absolutely tons of attention on GTA 6—there already is, if you haven't noticed—but not everyone plays GTA 6 and not everyone wants to watch videos or streams or read about it. There's no game so big it swallows absolutely everyone's attention for months, not even a new GTA game.

We've seen a lot of games getting out of the way of Rockstar's path, but pushing the release that far into 2027 suggests CIG just wants more time. And judging from the state of the recent disastrous Star Citizen livestream , it may need more time.

"I know a lot of you will be disappointed to not be playing Squadron 42 at the end of this year," Roberts said, "but it is the best thing for the project as it is truly something special and so needs to the opportunity to have the focus of the wider gaming world."

items.title: Where to find the Torrent skins in Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition
items.summary: Track down each Spectral Steed Regalia for Torrent.

content.v: The new Torrent skins in Elden Ring 's Tarnished Edition are tricky to find for bonuses that are meant to appeal to new players. It is FromSoftware we're talking about, though, so I can't say I'm exactly surprised they're a little tucked away. There are three Spectral Steed Regalias to find for Torrent in the Lands Between, plus new armor and weapons .
Spectral Steed Regalia: Tree Sentinel location
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Amgrn7yHksEgWGCfXbwcFX.jpg

You can grab this Torrent skin after you beat the demigod, Godrick the Grafted, in Stormveil Castle in Limgrave. After the boss is dead, open up the throne room, and head through the right-hand doorway behind the throne . Elden Ring players will likely remember that this room has always been empty, but now you'll find a chest containing the Spectral Steed Regalia: Tree Sentinel, which makes Torrent look like the aforementioned mounted boss.

After you have a Spectral Steed Regalia, you can change it at any site of grace. Simply select "change spectral steed appearance" and pick the one you want. If you already have an Elden Ring character, or aren't making a new one for Tarnished Edition, you should be able to backtrack and grab this chest even if you defeated Godrick many, many moons ago.

You can find the Carian Silver skin for Torrent in Ranni's Rise in north Liurnia of the Lakes. It's in a chest in the main downstairs room, right by the site of grace. Obviously, you'll have to defeat Loretta in Caria Manor to get here, but otherwise it's easy to grab. This skin makes Torrent look like a Carian knightly steed.

items.title: Exterminauts Devs Talk Helldivers Comparisons And How It Separates Itself
items.summary: If you saw footage of Exterminauts come out of Gamescom this week, then you might have thought it bore some re

content.v: If you saw footage of Exterminauts come out of Gamescom this week, then you might have thought it bore some resemblance to Helldivers 2. The two games are both cooperative PvE shooters with an assortment of powerful weapons to use and creatures to battle, but the team at Behaviour Interactive believe Exterminauts stands out in several key ways.

Speaking to GameSpot at Gamescom, creative director Vincent Regimbart acknowledged that there are definitely similarities in the two games, but also a few key changes that help Exterminauts stand out.

"Our game is not war: It's work," Regimbart said. "It's a workplace that fights back. So there's a thematic difference that we don't want it kind of, to be too heavy on the player--to make it feel like everything is ominous and dire. You're just here to do your 9-5 and get back out."
Regimbart also said that the team felt like it could actually make some improvements to certain aspects of Helldivers, particularly regarding the progression system.

"There are mods to your weapons, there are passives, there are a lot of upgrades, and there are a lot of different paths that you can take with a particular build. So we're putting a lot more emphasis on that."
For more on Exterminauts, you can check out our full Gamescom preview and read about how the season pass is respecting dedicated players. The game comes to PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC in 2027.

items.title: CD Projekt Red 聘请了 Modder 来帮助《巫师 3》在新的重制版中看起来比以往更好
items.summary: CD Projekt Red enlisted the help of a modder to help make the newly revealed The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remast

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2021/05/31/firstwitcher011280jpg-7667b2-1622477139209.jpg
CD Projekt Red enlisted the help of a well-known modder to help make the newly revealed The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered look better than ever.

The community creator, who calls themselves HalkHogan, shared the news in an update post on the Nexus Mods page for their own The Witcher 3 HD Rework Project (HDRP) mod. This single PC mod alone has garnered more than 320,000 unique downloads and more than 1.6 million views, and it sounds like it caught CD Projekt Red's attention ahead of The Witcher 3 Remastered, too.

In their message, HalkHogan confirmed their involvement in CD Projekt Red's official remaster release, telling fans of their work that they'll no longer need to use HDRP. Instead, they suggest players check out their contributions in The Witcher 3 Remastered, instead.

"Hello, my Witcher friends!" the message reads. "It's been a while since the last news, and I would like to clarify any questions and confirm that I am cooperating with CDPR on the Witcher 3 Remaster, and my work will be officially available in the game on September 29th (on PC and consoles). HDRP will no longer be needed."

The modder confirmed that "almost all in-game characters, monsters, animals, vegetation, armors, and equipment for Geralt and Roach," as well as "a large part of the environment," have been reworked for The Witcher 3 Remastered. They added, "I've put a lot of effort into ensuring the highest quality. :)"

The Witcher 3 Remastered was officially announced at gamescom Opening Night Live (ONL) 2026. It's currently set to refresh a classic 2015 RPG for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S September 29, 2026, but it sounds like its more than just another small visual update. You can see everything you need to know about it here , and how you can download the upgrade here .

It's a good time to be a Witcher fan. Also revealed at gamescom ONL 2026 was a first look at the surprise The Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past. Following critically-acclaimed DLC releases like Blood & Wine, IGN's short time with the content left us excited to see more . You can see everything else the developer had to reveal for the expansion here .
For more, you can read about the base game's quietly revealed price increase . You can also check out why some players are excited for more Gwent .

items.title: 《王国之心》的故事变得如此复杂，野村哲也称史克威尔艾尼克斯聘请了一位博学者来保持情节的连贯性
items.summary: The lore of Kingdom Hearts is so expansive that Tetsuya Nomura says Square Enix hired a loremaster to keep its

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/15/kingdom-hearts-d23-panel-everything-announced-1786825722441.jpg
The lore of Kingdom Hearts is so expansive that Tetsuya Nomura says Square Enix hired a loremaster to keep its story cohesive.

Kingdom Hearts IV is officially set for a late 2027 release. In the lead-up to its highly anticipated launch, fans have been returning to previous games in the series, to the point where a collection of Kingdom Hearts titles became one of the highest-selling games on Steam following an extended gameplay trailer shown at D23 in July.

In total, there are 13 games in the Kingdom Hearts franchise, which have been released on a bevy of different platforms over the years. That’s a lot to play through, not to mention a lot of story beats to keep track of as you go.

This isn’t a player-specific problem; even the developers find themselves getting lost from time to time, as revealed by series creator Tetsuya Nomura during an August 2026 interview with Famitsu . In fact, the storyline is so convoluted that Square Enix hired a loremaster to keep everything cohesive and explain the plot to Disney.

“As the Kingdom Hearts series has continued, the number of characters has inevitably increased, and the story has become more complex,” Nomura said. “For example, with the newly announced anime series , the number of external people involved in the Kingdom Hearts series has increased, and explaining the settings and scenarios each time has become quite difficult.

“Fortunately, the staff working on the ‘χ series’ had someone who meticulously compiled and organized the settings of past Kingdom Hearts series in an easy-to-understand way, and he was also in charge of explaining the scenarios and settings to Disney. In fact, at the beginning of Kingdom Hearts IV's development, Disney requested that he compile the materials, so he officially joined the Kingdom Hearts IV team as a proofreader.

Nomura says this "proofreader" was in charge of communicating the overarching story to Disney. He's a popular staff member due to how thorough his is, as he breaks down story beats, characters, and lore using visual diagrams.

"He is well-liked because he explains things to Disney as clearly as possible, using diagrams and such. His role internally is to proofread the script," he continued. "He checks to make sure there are no inconsistencies between the current script and past settings. He was especially suitable for this project because the χ series is deeply involved. Some people might mistakenly think he's in charge of composition, but it's actually ‘proofreading.’”

Nomura’s answer also revealed an integral connection between Kingdom Hearts IV and the χ titles, a series of prequel games set during the Age of Fairy Tales. These games were primarily available on web browsers and mobile devices, but Nomura says that “even if you haven't played the smartphone version, don't worry, their personalities are depicted within [Kingdom Hearts IV]."

The fact that even Disney themselves needed a loremaster to help explain the Kingdom Hearts story is a hilarious anecdote; the plot is famously convoluted and overwhelming, to the point where we at IGN felt the need to make a video explaining the lore in just five minutes .

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

items.title: 《Elden Ring》更新补丁说明揭示了多年来最大的变化
items.summary: FromSoftware has delivered a surprise Elden Ring update, revealing the biggest changes its critically acclaime

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2022/03/04/elden-ring-rune-farm-1646401242502.jpg
FromSoftware has delivered a surprise Elden Ring update, revealing the biggest changes its critically acclaimed action-RPG has gotten in years.

The developer caught fans off-guard with lengthy patch notes today, detailing a list of buffs (and a few nerfs) for different weapons and playstyles across the game. It's a major update that arrived as FromSoftware prepares for the launch of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition for Nintendo Switch 2, as well as its accompanying DLC for other platforms.

What we have here is a laundry list of balance adjustments that get under the hood to tweak a variety of PvE and PvP tools. Based on the list of updates available on the Dark Souls developer's website , the last time we received patch notes of a similar length was back in October 2024, a few months after the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion released. That makes it not only one of the biggest updates the 2022 game-of-the-year winner has received in years, but what could be one of its final ones, too.

Generally, what Elden Ring players have to look forward to is a lot of buffs. The Firespark, Lightning, Chilling, Frenzyflame, and Deadly Poison Perfume Bottles, for example, got increased attack power across the board. The Smithscript Axe and Spear, as well as the Spear of the Impaler, also benefit from reduced stamina use and increased power for thrown attacks.

The August Elden Ring update also comes with increased guard boost and reduced weight for the Lordsworn's Shield, Briar Greatshield, Spiked Palisade Shield, and more. Others, such as the Wooden Greatshield, Cuckoo Greatshield, Redmane Greatshield, and Crucible Hornshield, also got increased guard boost.

Another big change hits everyone's favorite FromSoftware mechanic: parries. You'll now notice improved parry performance across the board, for example, with the developer also explaining it's reduced the time before certain actions can be performed when using things like Daggers, Curved Swords, and Small Shields post-parry.

The nerfs, meanwhile, hit the Gravitational Missile and Great Katana. The former has been altered so that its projectile will not explode upon impact with terrain, while the latter now suffers from increased damage when hit by other players during an attack. The update also squashed bugs related to the Great Katana weapon, as well as a few PC-exclusive glitches.

For a game that turned four years old back in February, Elden Ring is still going strong. How much juice is left in the tank remains to be seen, though, as FromSoftware is very much staying busy with other projects . The Duskbloods , for example, may be a Switch 2 exclusive , but judging by the reactions to its first network test , it could compete with the studio's other multiplayer experiences.

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition will keep the train rolling when it launches tomorrow, August 28, for Switch 2 owners, with all of today's updates in tow. The Tarnished Pack DLC – which includes the Heavy Knight and Idus Knight starting classes, three Torrent skins, and four new armor sets – will also release for other platforms tomorrow.

Today's update is out now for players across PC, PlayStation 4, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S. You can check out the full patch notes below. For more, you can read about the Elden Ring movie , which wrapped filming in July . You can also learn about the social media post that had fans hoping to return to the Lands Between for even more content.

items.title: 《Helldivers 2》的老板很高兴《GTA 6》在发布时跳过了 PC 版，并且立即没有在线版本
items.summary: Pretty much everyone expects the November launch of GTA 6 to dominate the world of entertainment — indeed that

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/06/25/ultimate-edition-saras-salon-02-1782379342733.jpg

Pretty much everyone expects the November launch of GTA 6 to dominate the world of entertainment — indeed that’s one of the reasons we have a September crush of video game releases. But according to the CEO of Helldivers 2 developer Arrowhead, there are two very good reasons why developers shouldn’t be too worried.

Speaking to IGN, Arrowhead boss Shams Jorjani said that the lack of a PC version of GTA 6 at launch, as well as the absence of whatever the next generation of GTA Online looks like, means there’s reason to believe games like Helldivers 2 retain their own space.

“Rockstar makes ridiculous, high-effort stuff and it's awesome that games like this get made,” Jorjani said. “On a selfish level I'm happy it’s not hitting PC right away, and that online isn’t dropping at launch. It means Helldivers 2 gets to keep crushing it in our own space, and is also why it won’t be the all consuming behemoth everyone’s worried about.

“Everyone in the industry right now is constantly pivoting strategies and obsessing over early player feedback just to survive. But Rockstar has the brand power to confidently take their time and run their classic play. They have the confidence and freedom to spend a decade doing things the old-school way because they know the core game will deliver. It’s going to raise the bar for sure.”

Of course, Helldivers 2 is also out on console (it’s a PlayStation Studios game and Sony owns the Helldivers IP), but the explosive co-op action game is particularly strong on Steam, where it retains a loyal and sizeable audience of fans even now, two-and-a-half years after launch.

You’d image that the launch of GTA 6 will have an impact on even PC games, but perhaps long-running Steam games that revolve around online play will prove more resilient than others. Let's remember: GTA 6 is a single-player game at launch. There's no online mode at all this November.

GTA 6 is also set for launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S only, which in 2026 feels like an odd release strategy but is in keeping with Rockstar’s playbook. Jorjani touches on this in his comment — Rockstar is perhaps one of the few video game developers around that can guarantee success even skipping PC. GTA 6 is just that big of a deal. There’s nothing like it.
Be sure to check out IGN’s GTA 6 official gameplay reveal live blog , where we’ll bring you all the news across the internet on today’s Netflix exclusive and beyond.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 reveal live coverage: breaking down the Netflix 'extended look' event
items.summary: We're cataloging everything we learn about GTA 6 from the Netflix reveal, as well as reactions from around the

content.v: After years of speculation and rumors, Rockstar has finally given us a deeper official look at Grand Theft Auto 6. (Unlike the various unofficial looks we've been getting courtesy of a certain vegetable .)
The GTA 6 "extended look" aired Thursday, August 27 on Netflix at 12 pm PDT. It'll be available on Rockstar's YouTube channel six hours after that time.

The 26-minute long video was a montage of gameplay clips, some very brief, others showing extended scenes from missions. Though there's still a lot we don't know, much has now been confirmed about GTA 6's gameplay—we're picking apart the details below.
GTA 6 is due out on consoles on November 19. There's frustratingly still no PC release date, and Rockstar is unlikely to speak on that anytime soon.
What we've learned from the leaks
Ahead of the official GTA 6 reveal, someone who goes by "Cyberleek" has been releasing gameplay clips that apparently come from a build of the game they have continuous access to.

I assume there's a control room somewhere in which suited lawyers are pointing at giant maps and saying "enhance," but Rockstar hasn't tracked down the leaker yet, and in the meantime, we've learned a lot about GTA 6's gameplay.
Here are some of the big details, with the caveat that we can't be sure exactly how recent Cyberleek's build is:
The GTA 6 reveal is 'rousing' and 'violent'
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/JMgbsscgCzhTqWEzZBs2SF.png
That's according to the descriptors Netflix has chosen for the reveal. According to the Netflix mobile app, the video will be 26 minutes long.

I still think it's quite poor form for Rockstar to make fans subscribe to Netflix to see the reveal of a game they've probably already preordered. Yes, we can all just wait six hours for it to be posted on YouTube (and realistically, it'll be ripped from Netflix well before that), but it's the principle of the thing.
PC Gamer's Andrea Shearon has reminded me that Hannibal is on Netflix—the brilliant NBC show with Mads Mikkelsen—so I guess that's what I'll be doing with the renewed subscription I didn't want.
We're 30 minutes away
It's almost time. The anticipation for this big reveal has perhaps been dulled by the leaks that preceded it, but I still find myself quite curious to see what Rockstar is going to show.

So far, we've gotten the impression that GTA 6 is going to be something of a hybrid between previous GTAs and Red Dead Redemption 2, and that may manifest in deeper ways than we've seen from the infamous vegetable's clips.

I don't expect to hear much, or possibly anything, about GTA Online, but even if it's omitted, the fact of its omission will be notable. Rockstar surely has big plans for its future, but given how closely GTA Online (and its roleplaying community in particular) is associated with PC gaming, I wonder if those plans will be withheld until the studio is ready to talk about the PC version of GTA 6 itself.
There are also rumblings about user generated content being a focus, and but I'm unsure if that will have anything to do with the singeplayer game—we'll see!
We open with a drug pickup gone wrong
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/4pxvXakti7zWfBTwbk587j.jpg

We've gone straight into gameplay with no preamble, which is nice. The reveal opens with Jason and Lucia arriving at a drug distributor for a pickup. Naturally, things go wrong: This kingpin has been betrayed by his partner, and police are incoming. A shootout follows.

The player is controlling Jason, and we see them use a dynamic cover system. A computer-controlled Lucia follows suit and takes cover, interestingly. It looks to me like a lot of custom, mission-specific scripting rather than a dynamic system, especially as the couple chats back and forth mid-action. There's a nice fluidity to the animations. At one point we see a slow-mo kill cam after Jason takes out one of the corrupt cops—very Max Payne.
Obligatory 'yes, you can pet the dog'
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/dPxJwHAx2KSjNrr53h2x2h.jpg
Lucia seems fun, Jason's a bit boring so far
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/bbUiDmWVezujteUCvEyNyf.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/v2CoQkHKYeQYUkyPh4apif.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/K54hnfbXcNkeQFr44JzviS.jpg
After the shootout, we cut to a moment in Jason and Lucia's domestic life. Jason's personality, so far, seems to be "doofus with a deep voice." Lucia's a bit more fun.

The portrayal of Jason and Lucia as a relatable couple—Jason in this scene tries to hurry Lucia's outfit picking along—juxtaposes a little strangely with the GTA universe's goofiness. While Lucia's changing, Jason flips on the TV and we see a couple parody ads, like the one below advertising a 30,000 calorie sandwich made by slaughtering a prairie's worth of animals.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/JgjiHVthbQEGC3hLMHM2gG.jpg
Yeah, Lucia's definitely the cool one
A few details we've noticed
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/vUPuc8Yv3pXVDK7Qon5RUA.jpg
There are recreational activities for days
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/e2FY7Mpfpb8CnKTKZkx8bf.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/maQaMw8SCaDSjBHSQAQp9R.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/p2RoQewnEUj5udFkjfgC9R.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/w527tNJWLPxwj8VHir4pwQ.jpg

There's a clip of Jason shooting hoops (which we've seen in the leaks), plus lots of other recreational activities: scuba diving, fishing, jet skiing, kayaking, dirt bike riding, base jumping from a tower, street racing, dancing at a club, making it rain in a strip club.
Here's what that mid-jump character swap looks like

More details and reactions to come, but as we continue to process what we've seen, how are you feeling about the reveal? Is it worth breaking out a console for (or buying one for way too much money if, like me, you don't have one) or are you going to watch from the sidelines for now?
The reveal closes with a bloodbath at a party

The final few minutes of the reveal show a condensed edit of a full mission in which Jason and Lucia are tasked with "babysitting" a big media executive, Andrés de León of Megamundo, playing security detail at a party.

The couple meets Andrés at the airport and drives him to Megamundo's new US headquarters for the party. Despite protests from his COO, Andrés hides away in a conference room to do blow with his friends.

As with the drug deal, things go tits up, and armed goons invade the party. Jason and Lucia have split up for this; we see Jason's perspective for most of it, and text messages between Jason and Lucia appear floating in space next to them as they chat during cutscenes.
It's a little unclear where the line is between cutscene and gameplay at some points. We briefly take control of Lucia, but then she's attacked, and suddenly we're Jason again.

There's more gun combat here, and with the caveat that this is obviously carefully staged gameplay footage, it looks nice. Jason uses a bit of bullet time for the final kills, and then we cut back to Lucia fighting her way out of the predicament we last saw. I get the impression that our point-of-view isn't going to be up to us whenever the mission storytelling demands it.
Nothing to say about GTA Online

I didn't expect Rockstar to mention GTA Online in this video, but it still feels worth noting that it didn't. GTA 6 is a singleplayer experience at launch, and there's been no substantial comment yet on what's going on with GTA Online. Perhaps we'll learn more whenever Rockstar announces the PC version.
The studio acquired the team that made the popular GTA 6 roleplaying mod FiveM, and it surely has big plans for multiplayer adventures in Vice City.
The map is apparently twice as big as GTA 5's
That's according to a YouTuber TGG , who was invited to Rockstar North before the reveal.

"The map is twice the size of GTA 5's map," TGC says. "Three times the size of Red Dead Redemption 2's map. Vice City itself is twice the size of Los Santos, and Vice City and its surroundings suburbs is 11 times bigger than Los Santos and its surroundings."

items.title: Rockstar Games 和佛罗里达州官员正在商讨如何将迈阿密打造成现实生活中的罪恶都市，以开展 GTA 6 的营销活动
items.summary: Florida officials and Rockstar Games are having conversations to turn parts of Miami into Vice City for Grand

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/06/18/jason-and-lucia-03-landscape-1781798123709.jpg
Florida officials and Rockstar Games are having conversations to turn parts of Miami into Vice City for Grand Theft Auto 6's marketing campaign.

As initially reported by The Miamian , Miami-Dade County has had formal conversations with Rockstar Games about a Grand Theft Auto 6-themed takeover of Miami to promote the upcoming game. The report initially noted that Rockstar was the one that approached Miami-Dade with its ideas, but the article was later edited to clarify the city was actually the one who submitted a pitch deck.

While no plans are officially in place yet, the ideas pitched by the city are wide-ranging, ambitious, and likely absurdly expensive. One such idea includes transforming a section of Miami International Airport to serve as a "welcome" area for Vice City, complete with Vice City signage, limited edition luggage tags, themed luggage carts, a photo backdrop, and even a display aircraft wrapped in the game's purple color scheme.

Officials also proposed various activations around Miami's beaches, parks, and ports, creating unique events with DJs, food, exotic vehicles, photo ops, drone shows, murals, and much more. Outside of actual events, there are even ideas to have Rockstar take over the city's busses and trains with Vice City branding on the actual locomotives and stations associated with them. On the smaller side, there was also a pitch for Vice City-branded manhole covers and utility boxes.

The city created a number of proposals that would actually permanently help Miami in the long term, such as the creation of more bus shelters, quality of life improvements for its parks, and more. One of the more unique suggestions included the construction of a "radio lab" at a library in downton Miami. This would give visitors access to recording and editing equipment to produce music, podcasts, and more.

In a statement to The Miamian, Carlos Suarez, a spokesperson for Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine Cava, confirmed that they've had conversations with Rockstar Games, but there are no concrete plans in place at the moment.

“Nothing has been formally agreed to or approved, and any idea would have to go through the appropriate review and approval process," said Suarez. "Given Miami-Dade's clear influence on the game, we think there could be a unique opportunity to generate revenue for the County while showcasing Miami-Dade to a massive audience.”

It wouldn't be surprising if Rockstar uses the city of Miami to promote GTA 6 as part of its expansive marketing campaign, but it seems unlikely that it would go forth with all of these ideas. Not only are they expensive, but they may not all make sense for what Rockstar is envisioning for its advertising campaign.

The final marketing push for GTA 6 will ramp up today when Rockstar premieres an extended look at the game on Netflix . If you don't have Netflix or simply don't have time to watch, IGN will be doing a live blog with all of the big news from Rockstar's reveal. Additionally, a few new details were revealed yesterday including tidbits about specific gameplay mechanics and Rockstar doubling its size in order to produce GTA 6 .
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Devolver Digital Reveals Its GTA 6 Competitor, And It’s A Remaster Of A Nonexistent Remake
items.summary: Few game companies are brave enough to go head-to-head with the release of Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 , but

content.v: Few game companies are brave enough to go head-to-head with the release of Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 , but that's exactly what publisher Devolver Digital is doing with the launch of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on November 19.

Billed as a "remaster of the second remake of the original monochrome action-platformer starring the most famous video game mascot of all time," Volvy's Adventure is actually almost none of those things. The original "Volvy's Adventure" doesn't exist. This isn't a remaster but an entirely new and original game. Volvy, while actually being Devolver Digital's tongue-in-cheek platformer mascot, is obviously not the most famous of "all time."

So what is Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, actually? It's a Game Boy Color-style 2D platformer coming to Steam from developer Doinksoft, the studio behind 2D sidescrollers like Gato Roboto and Gunbrella . Volvy himself is a rat-esque (I think?) creature with one big hand and one small hand.

Like any good platforming mascot, Volvy dashes and jumps through levels while collecting items (in this case, onions), bouncing on the heads of enemies, and battling bosses. Occasionally, Volvy transforms into a hulked out alter-ego called Swolvy capable of smashing through anything that gets in his way.

It's all a little absurd, but that's also what makes it fun. While much of the marketing and the entire premise of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed comes off as a meta-video-game-industry joke, the actual game on display in its debut trailer looks like a rollicking good time.

Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is immediately reminiscent of its Game Boy Color-era inspirations, with a vibrant art style, a popping soundtrack, and kinetic movement. Volvy can dash through the air with his giant fist, burrow underground, or hover like a helicopter using his tail, and the trailer shows how all these abilities can all be chained together.

GTA 6 will certainly be hogging the headlines when it releases in November, but the open-world crime simulator isn't everyone's cup of tea, is $80 (or $100) , and isn't releasing on PC at launch. Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, at only $5, offers a nice bit of counterprogramming then for those who are looking for something else to do November 19.
Surprisingly, Volvy isn't the only one bold enough to release on the same day as GTA 6. The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ Online, a port adding online co-op, is also releasing November 19.

items.title: 《Manor Lords》庆祝销量突破 400 万份，推出重大更新，让玩家有机会成为“牧牛大亨”
items.summary: It's a great time to be a cow farmer.

content.v: Manor Lords is on a roll—with the medieval management sim celebrating the monumental milestone of over 4 million copies sold across all stores. And to commemorate the good news comes its next major update.

The new Major Update 8 will add a bunch of new features and quality-of-life bumps to Manor Lords. Soon you'll be able to use apples to make cider, honey to make mead, and thresh easy-to-grow oats so you can feed both humans and livestock.
https://t.co/ny1eaB5rwv August 27, 2026

Speaking of, there's also the chance for players to become "a cow-herding mogul with the ability to breed and import bovine livestock" alongside the new benefit of being able to make little barns for your sheep to help them last through the cold winter months.

As an accomplished Manor Lords sheep farmer, this is music to my ears. I love my sheep more than I love the townsfolk I'm stuck with, so I'll gladly take advantage of any way to make their wooly lives a bit warmer and a lot more comfortable.

Other features include welcoming cheesemongers to the hamlet, who will "form the basis of a future cheese-related perk" (I'm going to start trading in charcuterie—just watch me). Alongside a new river map which is known as Wide Valley, "a verdant region ripe for lording over".

I've been looking for a reason to get back into Manor Lords for a while now. I didn't even fall out of love with it, I just felt as if my time managing the hamlet had run its course. But with all of this new content on the way, this may be exactly what I needed to spur on another medieval sim session.

It could also be an equally good time for those who've never checked Manor Lords out before, because it's also currently discounted on Steam thanks to a bunch of Hooded Horse bundles and one very generous Kingdom Come: Deliverance x Manor Lords bundle, with the game being 35% off for the next two weeks.

items.title: 我解决了侠盗猎车手5中的男性孤独症流行病
items.summary: Reach out to your fellow human beings. And give them piggybacks.

content.v: Men. What is wrong with them and how can they be fixed?

Philosophers and scientists have asked this for generations, but the problem has only become understandable—and tractable—with the advent of modern technology. They are lonely. Contrary to the popular aphorism, all men are islands, struggling to exist in tempest-tossed seas. I have tried to solve this before, at least for Franklin, Trevor, and Michael, by introducing Pokémon to Los Santos. This did not work, and only resulted in me beating Charmander to death in the street.

The gentlemen of GTA require human companionship, not magical pets. They must find in others what is missing in themselves. They must use the 2gether mod for GTA 5 , which allows you to approach random NPCs and adorn yourself with them like they are some kind of boa or backpack. This is what friendship is all about.

The good news is: the people of Los Santos are remarkably pliable. No one objects to hopping on your back, or assuming the lotus position in your cupped hands, and they are utterly unfazed by the chaos unleashed by all the mods I have previously installed: flying cars, ongoing gang warfare, and so on.

To test their quietude, I asked a hiker to nestle himself in my hands as I attempted to sprint through an intersection. He was utterly placid as we were struck by three cars in a row, his murmured 'om mani padmi hum'* unbroken as an expensive German car used our combined mass as a ramp by which it could enter heaven.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/4zBxLbnU9T8BfTRQwyi886.gif

It was a true friendship, but it had to end eventually. Satisfied by his invincible tranquillity, I returned him to the nature spot in which I found him. Setting him down, he wandered off into a bush. In the distance, a Winnebago caught the sun as it drifted into the sky.
*He didn't actually say this, but I like to imagine he did.

items.title: Xbox CEO Plays Coy About Whether Elder Scrolls 6 Will Skip PlayStation
items.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has suggested Microsoft could make more exclusive games again , but will The Elder Scroll

content.v: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has suggested Microsoft could make more exclusive games again , but will The Elder Scrolls 6 be among them? We still don't know, but that's the question the BBC asked Sharma at Gamescom this week. But first, Sharma discussed her thoughts generally about exclusives, and how every platform, in her estimation, needs some form of exclusive content to grow.

"We are increasingly going to be one of the largest platforms in the world. Every platform needs some form of exclusive experiences and content," she said. "And so, what we've shared is Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork [Revolution will be exclusive on console to Xbox]. We're going to do the best we can to continue to do that, all in context of the business being healthy, and so we have to balance that."

Pressed to say if it is a "priority" to make The Elder Scrolls 6 exclusive to Xbox on console, Sharma smiled and said, "It's a beautiful game." Sharma recently visited the developers at Bethesda and offered an update on how the game was progressing . During her visit, protestors came to Bethesda's offices to drag Sharma for her decision to lay off thousands of Xbox developers , including people working on The Elder Scrolls 6.
Due to these layoffs and other cuts, staffers at Bethesda are facing "crushing morale" and fears of more delays.

In terms of Microsoft's approach exclusive games going forward, the team has said it will honor existing agreements for Xbox-made games that were previously announced as multiplatform releases. The Elder Scrolls 6 was announced in 2018, but at the time, Bethesda did not confirm platform details. Microsoft acquired Bethesda in 2021, and documents from the Microsoft vs. FTC case said The Elder Scrolls 6 was not planned for PS5 .

Former Xbox boss Phil Spencer, for his part, said in 2021 that making games exclusive to Xbox is "not about punishing any other platform." He also alluded to the possibility of The Elder Scrolls 6 being exclusive to Xbox.

"In order to be on Xbox, I want us to be able to bring the full complete package of what we have. And that would be true when I think about The Elder Scrolls 6," he said. "That would be true when I think about any of our franchises."

Spencer spearheaded the effort to bring more Xbox games to rival platforms in a bid to make more money. He left Xbox earlier this year, and one of Sharma's first moves was to tell fans how important exclusives are to the business . Gears of War: E-Day, which launches this October, was reportedly planned for PS5 before Microsoft opted to make it exclusive on console to Xbox.
Despite being announced more than eight years ago, The Elder Scrolls 6 still has no release date or official details.

items.title: 有史以来最贵的 Xbox 已售罄，人们已经开始以数千美元的价格出售它
items.summary: Microsoft opened up preorders for its limited-edition 25th-Anniversary Xbox Series X, and within a minute, the

content.v: Microsoft opened up preorders for its limited-edition 25th-Anniversary Xbox Series X, and within a minute, the most expensive Xbox ever sold out. While units will likely make their ways into the hands of Xbox fans with deep pockets, it looks like scalpers have also snatched up units, and as you'd expect, they're expecting to make a big payday by flogging them on sites like eBay.

A quick look at the commerce platform reveals dozens of the rare Xbox Series X consoles have been listed, with prices ranging from $2,200 all the way up to an incredibly optimistic $27,426 by one seller in Australia--likely as a way to grab the top spot on eBay's search page. Microsoft opened up preorders with a $900 asking price for the console, so this is quite the jump. So far, it looks like quite a few of the consoles have been sold at the marked-up price, with several sales on eBay averaging between $1,900 to $2,300 per unit sold.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Xbox-Ebay.jpg?w=636

This is also an unpleasant reminder of the early years of the current console generation, as thanks to a semiconductor shortage, the Xbox Series X and the PS5 were hard to find. Scalpers using a variety of methods and programs were quick to snatch up restocks online and resold them, but supply chains eventually stabilized and access to the current console generation was easier--at least until a variety of factors saw their prices surge upwards last year, with no sign of relief in the immediate future.

This is also yet another thing that scalpers have ruined, as many hobbies has been impacted by hustle culture. The Pokemon Trading Card Game has been especially hard hit , as every new restock at retailers usually sees scalpers buy up all of the available stock. Not even Pokemon donuts are safe , as the recent Krispy Kreme collaboration attracted plenty of people looking to make a quick buck.

items.title: Arc Raiders 将在 10 月份的重大更新中添加相机模式，但一些粉丝需要更多证据来证明该游戏不会消失
items.summary: This would've been really cool eight months ago.

content.v: We're getting dribs and drabs of news about Arc Raiders ' upcoming major update which is scheduled for October. A new "high-level" challenge has been promised to returning players, alongside a frozen map full of new arcs, plus there'll also be the small addition of a photo mode.

"Time to remember your raids, cameras are coming to the Rust Belt in October," a new social media post reads. By the looks of things this will let players record all the weird, wonderful, and downright stupid antics they get up to during Arc Raiders sessions. The only problem is, well, that the games just aren't as enjoyable as they used to be.
New Camera gadget coming in the October update!This looks pretty cool honestly pic.twitter.com/65vcFbk0iW August 26, 2026

Arc Raiders has had its issues with cheaters for almost as long as it's been out. While PvE lobbies are still ok, PvP is a swamp of bad actors right now, and it's only been getting worse the more decent people leave, meaning cheaters take up a bigger portion of the playerbase. Some are even throwing themselves in front of friendly fire just so they can trigger a self-defense clause and murder without consequence, you just can't win against these guys.

So with all things considered, players aren't exactly overjoyed about photo mode when the house is on fire. "Using number keys as a heal bind [has] been bugged since near launch," one player says , detailing how borked their hotkeys are. "But sure, let's add a fucking camera!"
"We finally need proof that we can believe what we have been promised, not just some gimmick to string us along," another player adds.

The frustration with Arc Raiders is clear, but I have to say I don't think it's fair to completely write the October update off before we've been able to play it for ourselves. I think it actually makes sense that Embark hasn't given too much away far in advance, hype would peter out quickly otherwise. I'm actually really excited to see the October update for myself, I'd love for it to spur on another stretch of raiding.

That isn't to say, however, that the October update doesn't have a lot to prove. On release Embark promised a grand 10-year plan for Arc Raiders. It hasn't even been a year since then, and that promise seems to be teetering on the brink. October might be the developer's final chance to convince players that this game really does have enough to take it further, because I fear patience is running thin.
